intervals.label: operating
intervals.quote: Physicists observed the first proton-antiproton collisions produced by the Tevatron on Oct. 13, 1985.

intervals.label: shut down
intervals.quote: It took about a month to fully shut down the CDF detector, including time to remove its cooling fluids and gases.

name: CDF detector
notes: Placed at site:fermilab-cdf-collision-hall-b0 (the Tevatron B0 interaction hall), created by this owner (colliders-historical); coordinates on that site are campus-precision only, see the site record.

placements.locator: fnal.gov Tevatron Experiments: CDF page; the INSPIRE experiment record long_name identifies the detector's location as "B0"
placements.note: End date approximate: CDF was "completely shut down" about one month after the Tevatron's 2011-09-30 shutdown per the Fermilab shutdown-process page.
placements.quote: Physicists observed the first proton-antiproton collisions produced by the Tevatron on Oct. 13, 1985.

calorimeters.quote: CDF's calorimeter for measuring the energies of particles that interact electromagnetically ... is made of 23 layers of lead and light-emitting plastic, and its calorimeter for particles that interact via the strong force ... is made of 23 layers of steel and plastic.
calorimeters.value: 23 layers of lead and scintillating plastic (electromagnetic) and 23 layers of steel and scintillating plastic (hadronic) sampling calorimeters

muon_system.quote: The final layer of the detector is made up of muon detectors, which catch the signals of the muons that pass through the calorimeters, giving up only a fraction of their energy.
muon_system.value: Outer layer of muon drift chambers catching muons that pass through the calorimeters

solenoid_field.quote: A superconducting solenoid of length 4.8 m and radius 1.5 m generates a 1.4 T magnetic field.

total_mass.note: 1988 NIM overview paper instead states "5000 t"; not reconciled, see experiment record note.
total_mass.quote: The 4,500-ton detector sits more than four stories tall and is composed of more than 1 million individual detector elements.

tracker.quote: CDF excels at tracking particle paths, using 7 layers of silicon positioned closely around the beam pipe, and a large "wire" chamber around the silicon that records up to 96 position measurements for each particle produced in the collision.
tracker.value: 7 layers of silicon microstrip detectors around the beam pipe plus a large open-cell drift ("wire") chamber recording up to 96 position measurements per particle

summary.plain: A four-story-tall, roughly 4,500-tonne particle detector built around the point where Fermilab's Tevatron collided protons with antiprotons, used to trace and measure the particles produced.
summary.technical: General-purpose solenoidal collider detector: silicon microstrip tracking plus a large open-cell drift chamber inside a 1.4 T, 4.8 m long, 1.5 m radius superconducting solenoid; lead/scintillator electromagnetic and steel/scintillator hadronic sampling calorimeters (23 layers each); outer muon drift chambers.

technology.quote: The Collider Detector at Fermilab (CDF) is a 5000 t magnetic detector built to study 2 TeV ... collisions at the Fermilab Tevatron. Event analysis is based on charged particle tracking, magnetic momentum analysis and fine-grained calorimetry.
technology.value: General-purpose solenoidal collider detector with silicon and drift-chamber tracking, sampling calorimetry and muon chambers
